hint1: My tongue can be almost 50 cm long.
hint2: I have a one-of-a-kind spot pattern.
hint3: I’m the tallest land animal on Earth.
funFacts: A giraffe’s heart can weigh more than 10 kilograms, and it pumps blood all the way up its long neck.

hint1: I spend most of my day curled up asleep in a tree.
hint2: My diet is almost entirely bamboo, even though I'm not closely related to the black-and-white panda.
hint3: I have a bushy ringed tail and a reddish coat, and people sometimes call me a 'red cat-bear.'
funFacts: Red pandas use their bushy tails as blankets in cold weather and have a false thumb, an extended wrist bone, that helps them grip bamboo stems.
imageAttribution: Photo: Bernard Landgraf, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons

hint1: I live so deep underwater that the pressure would crush most other fish.
hint2: Out of the water, gravity makes me look nothing like I do in my natural habitat.
hint3: I've been voted one of the world's ugliest animals, and my saggy face is famous online.
funFacts: A blobfish's body is mostly a gel-like substance slightly less dense than water, letting it float just above the sea floor without wasting energy swimming.
imageAttribution: Photo: Alphama, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons

hint1: I'm the only mammal in the world completely covered in scales.
hint2: When I feel threatened, I roll up into a tight, armored ball.
hint3: I use a long, sticky tongue to slurp up ants and termites, much like an anteater.
funFacts: A pangolin's tongue can be longer than its own body, and it retracts into a pouch near its pelvis when not in use.
imageAttribution: Photo: Ari hidayat99, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons

hint1: I live year-round in cold Arctic waters.
hint2: Males of my species usually grow a single long, spiraled tusk.
hint3: That tusk is actually an overgrown tooth, and it's inspired centuries of unicorn legends.
funFacts: A narwhal's tusk is a canine tooth that can grow up to 3 meters long and is packed with nerve endings, possibly helping it sense changes in the water.
imageAttribution: Photo: The Public Domain Review, Public Domain, Wikimedia Commons

hint1: I lay eggs, even though I'm a mammal.
hint2: I have a soft, sensitive bill that I use to detect prey underwater.
hint3: I look like a mix of a duck, a beaver, and an otter, and the males among us have a venomous spur on their hind legs.
funFacts: When platypuses were first described to European scientists, many believed the pelt was an elaborate hoax stitched together from other animals.
